FAILURES AND ARRANGEMENTS.
[It must not be overlooked that in many cases creditors whose names are published in these lists hold security for their debts, sometimes for the full amount.]
AUSTIN, JOHN, builder and contractor, 127, Brighton Road, Balsall Heath, Birmingham.-The Official Receiver for the Birmingham district has now issued particulars under this failure, from which it appears that

789

the gross liabilities amount to £6,684 9s. 3d., of which £1,448 13s. is expected to rank against the estate for dividend. The assets are estimated to produce £433 19s. 11d., thus showing a deficiency of £1,014 13s. It appears from the report and observations of the Official Receiver that the debtor commenced business in 1882 at 44, Brighton Road, Birmingham, with a capital of £30. Subsequently he went to Sydney, New South Wales, returning to Birmingham in the latter part of 1887. He then joined a Mr. Pegram in partnership, and they traded in Brighton Road as builders and contractors. In 1889 they lost £100 on a house they erected. In 1893 they built twenty houses in Fulham Road, Stoney Lane, at a cost of £3,500. Afterwards the partnership was dissolved, and the debtor took over all the assets and liabilities. At the date of the dissolution of partnership Mr. Pegram owned a house in Brighton Road subject to a mortgage of £250, and it was agreed with a Mr. Webb that he should give a charge to Mr. Webb, and the debtor also agreed to give Mr. Webb a charge on 35 houses for £800. Mr. Webb was at that time a considerable creditor. The debtor continued trading until November of last year, when, being unable to dispose of his properties, he began to press him. He therefore called his creditors together, and offered a composition of 5s in the pound, which was accepted, subject to the debtor being able to find security; however, debtor was unable to do so, and the present proceedings were instituted. The debtor alleges his failure to have been caused through losses on contracts and void houses. The first meeting of the creditors interested under this failure took place at the offices of the Official Receiver on the 2nd inst., when, after a long discussion, it was resolved to appoint Mr. James Rhodes, chartered accountant, Birmingham, as trustee, to act in conjunction with a committee of inspection.

BENNETT, N. J., builder, Burslem.—Yesterday week, at the Hanley Bankruptcy Court, this debtor came before Mr. E. Tennant, Registrar, for his public examination. The statement of affairs showed gross liabilities £738 10s. 5d. and a deficiency of £146 17s. 6d. Mr. F. C. Mayer represented the debtor. The examination was formally adjourned, and a meeting of the creditors was held, when a proposition by the debtor to pay 10s. in the pound, one half in a month and the remainder within two months, was accepted by the creditors present.
